clue.text: Entertained in the morning, employed afterwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours
something employed has been used

explanation.surface: Someone describes a morning spent hosting and then a stint of work later on.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to keep someone entertained is to keep them diverted and smiling.

clue.text: Inventor of some dotty characters

parts.note: dotty means crazy on the surface, but here the characters are made of dots and dashes in a telegraph code

explanation.surface: Someone who created a cast of eccentric people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dotty' looks like 'mad'; it means literally made of dots.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: Samuel F. B. Morse devised the telegraph code of dots and dashes.

clue.text: Carol hired something to wear

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
let means rented out, hired

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol rented an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a name; it is the verb, to sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sleeveless vest or undershirt is one garment you might put on.

clue.text: Assume this person might be at Oxford

definitions.meaning: to put on clothing, as in assuming a robe

definitions.text: this person might be at Oxford
definitions.meaning: a university teacher, especially a fellow at an Oxford or Cambridge college

explanation.surface: A guess about someone being at Oxford University.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' looks like suppose; it is to put on a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to put on clothes, and an Oxbridge college tutor or fellow.

clue.text: Irish port — girl needs route

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
a route is a way to go

explanation.surface: A girl wants directions to an Irish harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: GALWAY is a city and port on the west coast of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the city lies on Galway Bay, on Ireland's Atlantic coast, and has a working harbour.

clue.text: Travel with food and become crazy

parts.note: to travel is to go
bananas are a food

explanation.surface: Taking a journey with snacks and losing one's mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an informal phrase for going wild or losing one's temper.

clue.text: Depart from the French avenue

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a French boulevard.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to go away from a place.

clue.text: A new place in Kent? It's in Hampshire

parts.note: Dover is a port town in Kent

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fresh town belongs to Kent, and is told it is in another county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent and Hampshire are counties in southern England; Andover is a market town in Hampshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Andover is a town in the English county of Hampshire, so the definition fits one item in it.

clue.text: They support evening activity in the household

definitions.text: They support evening activity in the household

parts.words: They support evening activity in the household
parts.note: evening is read as making even, smoothing creases out of clothes, and these stands hold the clothes up while that is done

explanation.surface: Something props up what the family does after dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evening' looks like the time of day; it is the act of making things even, as a pressing chore does to fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: these padded folding stands hold garments while a hot iron smooths them flat.

clue.text: Bird stuck in gate alas!

indicators.note: the letters sit wedged inside the phrase gate alas, spanning its two words

explanation.surface: Someone laments a bird caught fast in a gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small freshwater duck, a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Prisoner to hand around jam

parts.note: con is short for convict, a prisoner
to serve food is to hand it around to diners

explanation.surface: An inmate passes round a pot of preserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is part of the phrase for serving, not a containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a conserve is a fruit preserve, much like a jam.

clue.text: Flower people hiding under vehicle

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits beneath the first, as if tucked under it

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Someone finds a bloom where people are hiding beneath a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a clove-scented pink, a popular buttonhole bloom.

clue.text: More competent gambler

definitions.meaning: comparative of good: more skilful or able

explanation.surface: A wagerer who is more skilled than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the comparative of good, and one who places a wager.

clue.text: English fellow had a meal spread out

parts.note: a fellow is a man
to have eaten is to have had a meal

explanation.surface: An Englishman's meal is laid out across the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to issue or flow outward from a source.

clue.text: Unspoilt scenery Nathaniel found by northern river

indicators.note: says the second piece sits next to the first

parts.note: Nat is a short form of the name Nathaniel
the Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, in the north of England

explanation.surface: A man called Nathaniel discovers untouched countryside beside a river up north.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure flows through the Yorkshire Dales in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym in one sense: the natural world, countryside left untouched by people.

clue.text: They may get into hot water in the afternoon break

definitions.text: They may get into hot water in the afternoon break

parts.words: They may get into hot water in the afternoon break
parts.note: getting into hot water usually means getting into trouble, but here it is literal: little sachets dunked into a mug at teatime

explanation.surface: People who land in trouble during their mid-afternoon rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot water' as trouble is the false trail.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: porous sachets of leaves steeped in boiling water to brew a cuppa.

clue.text: Letters seen in LONDON, PARIS, …

parts.note: the city names are printed in upper-case letters, and the cities are also seats of government

explanation.surface: A list of city names printed in big type.
explanation.walkthrough: The two readings meet: the names are in upper-case type, and each city is a nation's seat of government.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: upper-case letters, and the chief cities of nations, share the one word.

clue.text: I sold silly objects to be admired excessively

indicators.note: silly suggests the words I sold are jumbled into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to selling some daft trinkets that people adore.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: figures or people worshipped beyond reason.

clue.text: Summit where you'll see Bill and me

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: Someone says the mountain top is where you will find the two of you.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the highest point or peak of something.

clue.text: Rumpus? Some feel empathy when turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry the run is read from bottom to top, turned upwards
only some of the letters of feel empathy are taken, a run inside the words

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out, and a few people feel sympathy as it flares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks EELEM from 'feel empathy'; 'when turning up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a confused scuffle or noisy commotion.

clue.text: Whip pet with as many appendages as lives!

definitions.text: pet with as many appendages as lives!
definitions.meaning: a cat is said to have nine lives, so a cat with nine tails fits the description

explanation.surface: A whimsical image of a household pet with a tail for every one of its lives.
explanation.walkthrough: Cats proverbially have nine lives; the old naval flogging whip had nine knotted cords.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a whip of nine knotted cords once used for flogging sailors.

clue.text: The aim is to finish

explanation.surface: Someone states their goal is simply to complete the task.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a goal or purpose, and the verb to conclude.

clue.text: Session at school to get shorter, we hear

indicators.note: says the word meaning shorten is only spoken, the entry sounding the same

parts.note: to lessen is to become smaller or shorter

explanation.surface: A school period that is about to be cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a period of teaching in a classroom.

clue.text: Holding the girl, father ran quickly

indicators.note: father is wrapped round the girl's pronoun, holding it inside

parts.note: dad is an everyday word for father
she is the pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A father scoops up his daughter and sprints off.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have rushed or sprinted, past tense.
